- distinction between reproducibility and replicability: "The differences lie mainly in whether every element of a given study must be done in exactly the same way in any effort either to

- repeatability: "The closeness of agreement between independent results obtained when the 
same study is replicated on identical test material or subjects, using the same measurement procedure, same observer, same measuring instrument, the same location and under the same conditions" (p.17)
"Repeatability is the closeness of agreement between independent results obtained when the same method is replicated on identical test material or subjects and under the same conditions" (p.28)

go beyond the specific research components noted above. This may include 
descriptions of hardware, software, programming code, and other details

Hi Amelia,
I’ve coded the first text, and I have a few comments and questions. Overall, I think the workflow in the Google Form is good. However, I encountered some difficulties when choosing the answers, so I wanted to share my concerns.
The text is about “Replications in the Behavioral and Social Sciences,” so for B1a. Which discipline(s) does the paper focus on? What do you think about this choice?

•	“Attempting to computationally reproduce previous findings using the same numerical data, known as analytical replication, […]” (p. 117)
•	“Analytical replication is a stepping-stone to learning about re-analyses where student-researchers not only computationally reproduce but also introduce changes to previous statistical methods and models.” (pp. 117–118)
•	“replication as an ideal research practice: a process of substantiating knowledge to make it more reliable and useful” (p. 120)
As you can see, the text does not clearly distinguish between replication and reproducibility.
